Hi Olivia — thanks again for the call earlier today. Quick recap and suggested next steps so we stay aligned on procurement and approvals.

Call recap (30-min discovery):
- Goal: 3-month inference pilot to validate cost/latency improvements for patient triage workflows.
- Primary technical contact: you + engineering lead (we have Samir in procurement on copy).
- Key commercial question: preferred payment/contract route (PO vs company card vs AWS Marketplace) and signatory chain.

Questions we need answered to move to an SOW + PO:
1) Preferred commercial path (PO or card)? If PO, who is the PO request owner and procurement portal contact?
2) Who is the economic buyer (approves budget) and who signs contracts (legal/CFO)?
3) Timeline for internal approval (target go/no-go date).

Proposed next steps:
- I will share a lightweight SOW draft + pricing estimate (attached separately) for a scoped 3-month pilot.
- Ben will outline a commercial onramp option (pilot milestones and acceptance criteria).
- If PO is preferred, we can prepare invoice templates and W9 to speed procurement.

Attachments to follow: SOW draft, pricing estimate, W9. If marketplace purchase is preferable (faster procurement), let us know and we can check our AWS Marketplace listing + procurement SKU availability.

Can you confirm the PO owner / signatory and your internal target date for approval? If easier, propose a 15-min call with your procurement contact and Ben to walk through the PO paperwork.

Thanks — Jasmine

Thanks, Jasmine — useful recap. A few clarifications from my side: 

1) Procurement path: Novaterra prefers a PO route for pilots > $5k. For smaller items we can use a company card, but for something that touches infra and vendor contracts we go through PO + PO number. We are evaluating whether Marketplace is acceptable (some teams prefer it for speed), but Legal typically prefers a PO + MSA.

2) Budget & signatory: The budget resides with Samir (Head of Finance, cc'd). Final signatory for standard tech MSAs falls to our CFO, Clara Mendoza (clara.mendoza@novaterra.com). Procurement will route through our vendor portal (I can introduce you to our portal admin).

3) Timeline: We're aiming to approve pilots in the week of Mar 15 but could accelerate to early Mar if procurement has the docs early.

I've attached our initial RFP scan (Novaterra-RFP-Scan.pdf) that lists some compliance items Legal cares about. Please send the SOW + W9 + pricing so Samir and I can forward to procurement.

Subject: Commercial onramp & PO-friendly billing options

Olivia — appreciate the clarity. Short note on approach from commercial side and how we typically route PO customers: 

High-level onramp (recommended for Novaterra):
- Phase 1 (Pilot, 3 months): Dedicated pilot capacity with SLOs for latency for triage flows. Acceptance criteria: throughput benchmarks + sample eval set.
- Phase 2 (Expansion): Scale to production endpoints, optional Dedicated pools or Marketplace procurement depending on preference.

Procurement & billing options we support: 
- PO / Invoice: Net 30, monthly invoicing. We provide a W9 and our standard MSA + SOW. Procurement portal friendly: we can generate a vendor record package (W9, MSA, bank remit details).
- Card: Immediate access for small engagements; billing via card is supported for self-serve hosted API.
- Marketplace (AWS): Can be faster for procurement and procurement teams sometimes prefer marketplace SKUs; note that marketplace contracts can add billing constraints and affect our refund/credits process vs direct PO.

If you confirm PO is preferred, we can:
1) Send Redwood-W9.pdf + a redlined MSA template and the SOW draft (attached)
2) Provide a price sheet (attached PriceEstimate) scoped to the pilot (token estimates + Dedicated pool hours)
3) Offer a short procurement kick-off call — I can be on the call to walk your procurement admin through the invoice template and vendor setup.

Next steps: Jasmine, can you propose 2x 15-min slots next week for an intro call with Novaterra procurement? Olivia / Samir — please confirm preferred billing method (PO confirmed here) and whether procurement prefers the vendor package as a zipped bundle or a ShareDrive link.

Ben Carter
